practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Each test should focus on a single requirement/behavior. RATIONALE: Enables precise root cause identification. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Check number of distinct 'Act' operations or multiple Arrange-Act-Assert blocks. DECISION RULES: The method performs repeated calls to a single public operation (fila0.enfileira) to exercise a single behavior (overflow). There is one overall Arrange-Act-Assert flow (setup, loop act, final assertions). VERDICT: compliant because the test targets a single behavior (queue overflow) with one logical Arrange-Act-Assert pattern even though the act is repeated.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be independent and do not rely on other tests. RATIONALE: Ensures deterministic, order-independent execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for @Before/@After or shared mutable state. DECISION RULES: This test uses only local variables and does not reference or mutate static/instance state. No test-order naming. VERDICT: compliant because it is self-contained and does not depend on external test state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should cover both normal (happy) and error flows. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and handling of edge conditions. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Need at least a happy path and an error-case test for methods. DECISION RULES: The test class contains only one test method (this method) and exercises an exceptional flow (overflow) only; there is no separate happy-path test verifying normal enqueue/dequeue behavior. With only a single test method, it fails to provide both flows. VERDICT: non-compliant because the class lacks a separate happy-path test for enqueue/dequeue.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should check min/max and off-by-one cases. RATIONALE: Boundaries are frequent error sources. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for empty, zero, negative, max, min, or just-inside/outside inputs. DECISION RULES: The test exercises repeated enqueues up to a SAFE_LIMIT and checks for overflow, but does not explicitly test boundary values such as empty queue dequeue, single-item behavior, zero or one-element boundaries, or off-by-one enqueue beyond capacity. VERDICT: non-compliant because it lacks explicit boundary inputs (empty/dequeue, zero/one element, just-before/after capacity).

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helpers/constants. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and improves readability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for helper methods, constants or short tests without repetition. DECISION RULES: The method defines a local constant SAFE_LIMIT and follows Given-When-Then comments; there is no duplicated code across multiple tests (class has one test). VERDICT: compliant because the test demonstrates modular structure (local constant, clear structure) and no duplicated logic across methods is visible.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and avoid loops/complex conditionals. RATIONALE: Simpler tests are easier to reason about and less error-prone. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Tests should be <20 lines and avoid loops/complex conditionals. DECISION RULES: The test contains an explicit for-loop (for (int i = 0; i < SAFE_LIMIT; i++)) which increases cyclomatic complexity; presence of loops in the test body triggers non-compliance. VERDICT: non-compliant because the test contains an in-method loop, which increases complexity and makes the test longer/more complex than ideal.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive to detect faults. RATIONALE: Superficial assertions may miss faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Prefer multiple property checks; more than one assertion is better. DECISION RULES: The test has a single assertTrue checking the exception message contains particular words. That is a single, somewhat superficial assertion; it does not verify exception type, that overflowObserved is true via assert, or other properties. VERDICT: non-compliant because only one assertion (message contains) is used; more comprehensive assertions would improve fault detection.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be actively maintained without ignored/disabled tests. RATIONALE: Disabled tests hide regressions. EVALUATION CRITERIA: No @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test. DECISION RULES: There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out tests in the provided method. VERDICT: compliant because the test is active and runnable with no disabled/commented test code.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be specific and include messages. RATIONALE: Specific assertions help diagnose failures. PRINCIPLE: Comments should add value and explain why, not what. RATIONALE: Excessive comments clutter tests; minimal useful comments are acceptable. PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid sources of non-determinism. RATIONALE: Flaky tests erode confidence. practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests must not create lasting side effects or shared state changes. RATIONALE: Side effects create inter-test dependencies.
